text: {"observations":"The clip is dense music with a strong bass (peaks near 52 and 107 Hz), but a harmonic melodic line runs through it. Its fundamental sits around 220 Hz (A3) from about 2 to 6 s, with harmonics at about 440, 660, 880, 1100, 1320 and 1540 Hz. The line glides rather than stepping cleanly: about 246-260 Hz at 0-1 s, about 234 Hz at 6.1 s (third harmonic near 706 Hz), then a slide from about 186 up to 199 and back to 220 Hz at 6.5-6.9 s (third harmonic moving 557 to 598 to 660 Hz). These continuous pitch glides and small wobbles (870-890 Hz on the fourth harmonic) suggest a sung voice rather than a fixed-pitch instrument, which argues against D. The sung range of roughly 185-260 Hz (G3-C4) is typical of a male singer and low for a female or child voice, so B is favoured over A and C. The evidence is indirect, so this is a best estimate rather than a certainty.","answer":"B"}
